title: Check command: run it from the project's own folder when the project lives in a subfolder of its repo (monorepo)
lead: *Proposed.* Drafted 2026-11-09 at HEAD 4707be4. Size S recommended. Status: READY. Owner decision 2026-11-07: infer the check folder from the project path relative to the repo top level; no new setting; the slice is narrowed to the working directory only (S294's stall rule already covers repeated output). S295 reuses the helper this slice adds.
findings_note: 2026-11-05, prism-ui (libraries/prism-ui inside the platforms repo): the configured check 'dotnet build PrismUi.slnx ...' ran from the worktree root and failed MSB1009 on every round, so U41 burned all 8 fix rounds on a red check no code change could fix (the implementer said so in rounds 2 to 7). Wanted: run the check with the project's subfolder as the working directory, or stop fix rounds when the same check output repeats unchanged after a no-change implementer report. Also: 'ork projects set' refuses while any run is unfinished, so the owner could not fix the config mid-wave; a stopped run counts as unfinished.

sections.heading: Why
sections.body:
- Evidence 2026-11-05, prism-ui (`libraries/prism-ui` inside the platforms repo): the check `dotnet build PrismUi.slnx ...` ran from the worktree root and failed `MSB1009` on every round; U41 spent 8 fix rounds on a red check no code change could fix.
- Correction on the S293 record, 2026-11-05: a stopped run does not block `ork projects set` (`runrec.IsFinal`, `internal/runrec/record.go:39`). That part is not in this slice (see S296).
- Code at HEAD: `runChecks` calls `check(ctx, rec.Worktree, cmd, timeout)` twice (`internal/engine/states.go:361-379`, once and again on a failure, S239) and `RunCheck` runs `sh -c` in that `dir` (`internal/engine/check.go:19-20`). `rec.Worktree` is `.worktrees/{id}` under the project path (`worktreePath`, `internal/engine/engine.go:140-150`) created with `git worktree add` from `e.proj.Path` (`internal/engine/states.go:899`), so it is a full checkout rooted at the repo top, not at the project's folder.
- `runChecks` is used by the round check (`states.go:235`) and by the landing re-check (`internal/engine/land.go:190`); both change together.
- Overlap: S295 (verify the check where it will run) says "Not S293 (which directory)" and wants one helper for the directory; S294 (done) owns the repeated-output stall. `slicer --root ../slicer find monorepo` finds s240 (reports on nested projects), unrelated.
- Not verified and out of scope by the owner's narrowing: `slicer check` and `slicer show` also run in `rec.Worktree` (`states.go:384`, `:640`, `:805`); whether slicer finds the project root from the repo top in a monorepo was not examined.

### Open questions

1. How is the folder inferred? Options: (a) `git rev-parse --show-prefix` in the project path (recommended: git's own answer, handles symlinks, no path arithmetic); (b) `--show-toplevel` and `filepath.Rel`. Key: `engine.check-dir-source`.
2. Say the directory in the check log? Options: (a) yes, one line `(in REL)` only when the folder is not the repo root (recommended: the owner sees where it ran, and S295 names the directory too); (b) no. Key: `engine.check-dir-log`.
3. The project folder is missing in the worktree: (a) pause with an error naming it (recommended); (b) fall back to the worktree root. Key: `engine.check-dir-missing`.

sections.heading: Failing tests
sections.body:
- `TestCheckDirIsTheProjectFolderInAMonorepo` (`internal/engine`, real temp git repo): repo top `R`, project at `R/libraries/p`. `git rev-parse --show-prefix` in the project gives `libraries/p/`. For worktree `W`, assert `CheckDir` returns `W/libraries/p`. Fails first: the helper does not exist and `runChecks` uses `W`.
- `TestCheckDirIsTheWorktreeRootWhenTheProjectIsTheRepoRoot`: prefix empty; returns `W`.
- `TestRunChecksRunsTheCommandInTheProjectFolder`: with the monorepo harness, a check `pwd > out` run through `RunCheck`; assert the recorded directory is `W/libraries/p` in the round check, in the S239 rerun, and in the landing re-check (`land-checks`).
- `TestCheckDirMissingInTheWorktreePausesWithAReason`: the project folder does not exist in the worktree; the run pauses with kind `error` and a reason naming the directory (not a silent fallback to the root).
- `TestCheckDirReadErrorPausesWithAReason`: `git rev-parse --show-prefix` fails; pause with the git error.
- `TestCheckLogNamesTheDirectory` (only if Q2 option a): the check log starts with `$ cmd` and a line `(in libraries/p)`.
- Existing check tests keep passing unchanged for a project at the repo root.

sections.heading: Implement
sections.body:
1. Add `CheckDir`: `git -C PROJECT_PATH rev-parse --show-prefix` through the engine's `gitRead` (`internal/engine/round.go:87`), then join the trimmed prefix to the worktree path. An empty prefix gives the worktree.
2. Use it in `runChecks` for the project command only. Keep `e.d.Slicer.Check(ctx, rec.Worktree)` as it is.
3. Do not add a setting, do not change `check_command`, `check_minutes`, the S239 rerun, the S294 stall rule, or `ork projects set`.
4. Leave S295's verification to S295; name the helper in its Files list when S295 is specified (S295 reuses it).
5. Docs and CHANGELOG, marked *proposed*.

Owner decisions (2026-11-09, accepted the recommended answers): How is the folder inferred? -> (a) `git rev-parse --show-prefix` in the project path (recommended: git's own answer, handles symlinks, no path arithmetic) [engine.check-dir-source, adj 211]. Say the directory in the check log? -> (a) yes, one line `(in REL)` only when the folder is not the repo root (recommended: the owner sees where it ran, and S295 names the directory too) [engine.check-dir-log, adj 212]. The project folder is missing in the worktree -> (a) pause with an error naming it (recommended) [engine.check-dir-missing, adj 213].

sections.heading: Check
sections.body:
- `go test ./...`
- `go vet ./...`
- `gofmt -l .`
- `slicer check`
- `adj lint`
- No `internal/tui` or CLI output change unless Q2 option a puts a line in the log; the log is a file, so no UI pass (rule u10).
- [HUMAN CHECK] On a project inside a monorepo subfolder (prism-ui), start a small run: the person confirms the check log shows the command succeeding from the project folder.
